messages:
sophie: heads-up — multiple customers reporting p99 spikes on text-generation since ~03:20 UTC. support ticket ids 9871, 9890. example: customer 'atlas-ai' saw p95 jump from ~110ms -> ~480ms and p99 from ~420ms -> ~1.7s. they sent trace id tr-atlas-0001.

maria: thanks. did we roll anything last night? kernel/driver/firmware?

deploy-bot: recent infra changes: 2024-11-07 02:18UTC - rolled kernel 6.3.1 -> 6.4.0 to canaries (asg-canary-3), 02:42UTC - promoted nvidia-driver 535.112 -> 545.23 to nodes in eu-west-1a.

ajay: seeing the same on our dashboards. p95 across serving fleet jumped at 03:15 UTC. quick numbers: baseline p95 ~120ms -> 420ms, p99 baseline ~380ms -> 1.6-1.9s. error rate normal. CPU okay, GPU utilization down slightly, NVMe tail latency up. linking perf graph: https://obs.redwood/internal/d/latency/serving-p95 (perf-bot posted snapshot). :eyes:

perf-bot: snapshot: panels -> p95 and p99, nvme queue depth, kernel errors. (https://obs.redwood/snapshot/abc123)

liam: suggests it's storage/host-level. last night kernel bump + driver bump matches timeline. NVMe tail latency spiking is a classic host-kernel vs NVMe doorbell interaction. can someone grab dmesg / nvme smart logs from one affected host?

maria: grabbing node i-0a12f3 (eu-west-1a). run these and paste output:
```
sudo dmesg | tail -n 200 | egrep -i "nvme|I/O|timeout|nvme0"
sudo nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0
iostat -x 1 10
sudo journalctl -u redwood-inference --since "2024-11-07 02:00" | grep -i latency | head -n 200
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,utilization.gpu,fan.speed --format=csv
```

sophie: posted customer trace (redacted) — they repro with a short burst of 50 concurrent requests to the v2/generate endpoint, sequence length ~512. gave them quick curl for repro:
```
for i in {1..50}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Request-ID: tr-atlas-0001-$i" -d '{"model":"redwood-rlhf-1","input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood/v2/generate &
done
```

ajay: captured iostat & nvme logs from i-0a12f3: (summary)
- avg await for nvme0: 0.8ms -> spiking to 12-180ms in bursts
- util low, but svctm shows long tails
- dmesg shows repeated: "nvme nvme0: I/O 12345 timeout, qid 8" and occasional "Reset controller due to handler"

liam: that matches kernel/driver incompat between nvme driver and newer kernel scheduler. also saw increased flushes after driver 545 introduced new NVMe multi-queue handling.

maria: immediate mitigations we can try:
- rollback nvidia-driver on a small canary ASG to 535.112 (fastest)
- for nodes where kernel 6.4 applied, boot them back to 6.3 from rescue image (if available)
- temporarily increase NVMe queue depth and adjust read-ahead on affected hosts
- route critical customers to older pool (dedicated nodes still on 6.3/535)

ajay: operational plan:
1) isolate canary ASG (asg-canary-3) and drain traffic
2) perform driver rollback + reboot
3) run stress repro (sophie's curl) from internal runner and watch p95/p99 for 30m
4) if good, roll to other ASGs in eu-west-1a in small batches
5) if rollback not effective, revert kernel boot or contact NVMe vendor/host to escalate firmware/host settings

liam: rollback commands (on AMI images using apt/yum):
```
# example for ubuntu deb package
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535=535.112-1
sudo update-initramfs -u
sudo reboot
```

Or using our image-bake flow: `infra/ami-bake --rollback-driver 535.112 --region eu-west-1a --asg asg-canary-3`

sophie: customers asked for ETA. what can we offer as a mitigation quickly?

maria: short-term customer-facing mitigations:
- switch heavy customers to dedicated pool (we have capacity in dedicated-eu-west) — takes ~3-5m to re-route via routing rules
- offer credits and status updates: support should message customers: "We're investigating elevated p99 latency; temporary routing to more stable pool can be applied immediately. Engineers are performing targeted rollbacks now."

sophie: I'll message atlas-ai with that and offer to move them.

deploy-bot: rollback job queued: infra-job-1599 by maria on asg-canary-3. ETA ~8m.

ajay: started repro run on canary after rollback. initial 10-minute window shows p95 back down to ~130ms and p99 ~480ms (still slightly above baseline). we'll keep running 30m; if stable we'll proceed to next ASG.

maria: good — also opened ticket to cloud vendor asking for nvme firmware logs (ticket CV-4521). included dmesg excerpts and SMART logs.

liam: post-rollout checks:
- grep for vfio/nvme errors in dmesg
- monitor nvme tail latency graphs and queue depth per-instance
- run full load test with sequence length 1024 (to exercise larger KV cache)

ajay: note — we observed cold-start penalty on instances after rollback (likely due to driver re-init) causing transient 10-20s token latency in a few traces; added a warming script to pre-populate KV cache:
```
python tools/warm_kv_cache.py --addresses $(cat canary_hosts.txt) --model redwood-rlhf-1 --batch 8
```

sophie: customer update sent for atlas-ai: "We've identified a host-level storage interaction after last night's infra updates. We've routed you to a stable pool and initiated rollbacks. We're monitoring and will follow up in 30m with status." They replied :thumbsup:.

ajay: 30m post-rollback summary: canary stable, p95 ~125ms, p99 ~460ms. some stray hosts still show intermittent nvme timeouts; marked those for repro and isolate. we should keep kernel/driver pinned until we verify vendor fixes.

maria: long-term action items (tracked in infra ticket INF-3342):
- coordinate with NVMe vendor for firmware patch and validate on testbed
- add canary gating to prevent promoting kernel+driver changes together (enforce separate promotions with 24h gap)
- add automated NVMe health checks and alert on queue-depth skew
- improve rollback automation to reduce KV-warm penalty (warm after rollback automatically)

liam: also propose adding a runtime fallback policy: if nvme tail > 100ms for 5m, route high-priority traffic to model-variant that uses smaller KV cache footprint (or CPU fallback) until resolution.

sophie: assigning follow-ups: maria -> rollbacks & vendor ticket, ajay -> full fleet health check + isolate bad hosts, liam -> runtime fallback PR, sophie (support) -> customer comms and credits.

maria: will update infra status page and post a postmortem draft once we have vendor root cause. keeping this thread pinned.

ajay: closing loop here — if anyone sees fresh customer escalations please ping me directly. thanks all. :pray:
